headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: transformers can read/write broad local files while argo-workflows can move artifacts over APIs, creating unsafe default pairwise pipelines.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A can expose artifacts through REST/gRPC and B can read files and parse text, images, and scripts. That creates a plausible default path where B ingests A-produced content as instructions or data. No shared channel is explicitly documented, so this is inferred from the profiles and uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF A writes attacker-controlled content into a shared artifact path that B later reads
IF B treats file contents as trusted instructions or prompts
mitigations: Add a strict content-type allowlist for files passed from A to B
Insert a manual review step before B consumes A outputs
Store A outputs in a quarantine directory with read-only access
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to every artifact
requires-engineering: isolate the two agents into separate workspaces

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches artifacts and parameters and has allowlisted network egress; B has broad network egress plus filesystem read/write. If they share a workspace, B can read A outputs and transmit them onward. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so I keep this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF A and B share any filesystem or mounted workspace
IF A outputs contain sensitive artifacts or parameters
IF B forwards those files or derived text to a remote endpoint
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories or volumes
Disable B network egress for runs that touch A outputs
Redact sensitive parameters before A emits artifacts
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls on shared storage
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning before any upload

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A can call APIs and B can execute shell, install packages, spawn subprocesses, and write the filesystem. If they operate on the same mutable workspace, concurrent writes or API-driven side effects can collide and corrupt state. Because the profiles do not show locking or isolation, uncertainty escalates to high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or repository
IF A's API actions and B's shell actions target the same mutable resource
IF no external lock or transaction guard is present
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate workspace
Serialize access with a simple lock file
Make B operate read-only when A is active
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks
requires-engineering: route writes through a single orchestrator

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces workflow artifacts and B can execute shell and write files, so B may treat A output as authoritative and act on it without verification. That is a classic pipeline cascade: one bad artifact from A can trigger downstream actions by B. The profiles do not document a verification gate, so the safer high severity applies.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated artifacts or text without validation
IF B performs file writes or shell actions based on A output
IF A output contains an error, malicious instruction, or malformed schema
mitigations: Add schema validation before B consumes A output
Require human approval for any B action derived from A
Log and diff A outputs before execution
requires-engineering: add checksum-based handoff validation
requires-engineering: separate generation from execution stages

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch in the profiles. I therefore see only a limited compliance gap: B handles richer data classes than A, but the pairwise evidence does not show regulated data or a jurisdiction conflict. One citation per agent is sufficient because the issue is profile-level, not interaction-specific.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is routed through B
IF the deployment imposes retention or residency rules not met by the host environment
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to B
Avoid regulated data in this pair unless controls are documented
Review retention settings on the host platform
requires-engineering: document residency and retention guarantees
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for sensitive datasets
